verdict.rationale: First-party ecosystem components give the assistant a real execution surface. Open Terminal lets the AI install dependencies, write an app, start its server and inspect the output. Open WebUI Computer runs on the user's machine and exposes files, terminal and editor, while Tether brings local files and tools into chat with an optional workspace sandbox, which is real isolation rather than a dry-run. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of file-edit and command-approval flows (each capability is a single-line mention), and independent hands-on corroboration of exec on the user's own machine beyond a passing community mention of code execution.

support.subject: As a power user, the assistant can run commands and edit files on my machine — a real exec surface, not just chat about what to do

citations.quote: Your AI can install dependencies, write the app, start its server, and inspect the output.
Open WebUI Computer (`cptr`) runs on your machine and serves your whole computer to any browser: files, terminal, editor, git, browser tabs, running sessions, AI agents, and tools.
It brings your files, tools, and local models into chat, with an optional workspace sandbox to choose where the AI can work.
Run Python directly in the browser or via Open Terminal
